text: “But, of course, you know all about these things, and you have Mr. Vyse to help you. A gentleman is such a stand-by.” Mrs. Honeychurch, who had come up to town with her daughter, began to drum nervously upon her card-case. “We think it so good of Mr. Vyse to spare you,” Miss Catharine continued. “It is not every young man who would be so unselfish. But perhaps he will come out and join you later on.” “Or does his work keep him in London?” said Miss Teresa, the more acute and less kindly of the two sisters.
